about.title: Lafayette Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a traffic collision changes everything, and Lafayette families are not immune to that pain. Public records show the city logs roughly 106 injury collisions a year, with crashes tending to cluster on Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m. along corridors like SR-24. When one of these collisions turns fatal, California law allows certain surviving family members — typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, followed by other dependents or heirs — to pursue a wrongful death claim. This is a civil action, separate from any criminal proceedings the responsible party may face. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we connect families in Lafayette with an independent personal injury attorney who can review what happened, explain the strict filing deadlines, and help pursue compensation for funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of companionship no dollar figure can truly replace. The consultation is free, and there's no fee unless the attorney recovers on your behalf.

items.title: Only Certain Family Members Can File
items.desc: California limits wrongful death standing to specific people, typically a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents or heirs eligible in some cases. An attorney can help determine where you fit.

items.title: The Clock Starts at Two Years
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death claim in California, though claims against a government entity carry a much shorter deadline. Missing it can end your ability to recover.

items.title: Recoverable Losses Go Beyond Bills
items.desc: California law allows families to seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and compensation for the loss of a loved one's love, companionship, and guidance — losses that are real even when they're hard to quantify.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim after a Lafayette crash?
items.answer: California law generally gives priority to a surviving spouse, registered domestic partner, or children. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may have standing depending on the family's circumstances. An independent attorney can review your situation and confirm who qualifies.

items.question: How long do we have to file after losing someone on SR-24 or another Lafayette road?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of death to file a wrongful death lawsuit. If a government agency's road design or maintenance may have contributed, that deadline can be much shorter, so it helps to act quickly.

items.question: Does a wrongful death claim happen separately from any criminal charges against the driver?
items.answer: Yes. A wrongful death claim is a civil case pursued by the family, entirely separate from any criminal prosecution of the at-fault driver. The two can proceed on different timelines and don't depend on each other's outcome.

items.question: What does LawProactive actually do for families in Lafayette?
items.answer: We're a free connection service, not a law firm, so we don't represent you directly. We simply match your situation with an independent personal injury attorney in the network who handles wrongful death cases on a contingency basis, meaning no fee unless there's a recovery.
